0.0.n: Combines with の人 to make 女の人, a common way to say woman.

0.1.n: Links 女 to 人, describing the person as female rather than showing ownership.

0.2.n: 女の人 as a whole refers to a woman.

0.3.n: Marks the woman as the topic: the sentence tells us what she did.

0.5.n: 男 refers to the male character receiving the food and tea.

0.6.n: Marks the man as the recipient of what the woman serves.

0.7.n: Names one of the two things the woman serves.

0.8.n: Joins two nouns, 食べ物 and お茶, into a list.

0.9.n: The お is a customary polite prefix; お茶 is the usual everyday word.

0.10.n: Marks both food and tea as the things being served.

0.11.n: 出す in its て-form plus くれました makes the action a favor; ました marks polite past tense.

1.0.n: Refers to the same male character introduced in the previous sentence.

1.1.n: Marks the man as the topic, shifting attention to his reaction.

1.2.n: 安心 combines with する to describe feeling at ease; しました is the polite past form of する.

0.lit: As for the female person, she served food and tea to the man as a favor.
0.tip: てくれる presents an action as a favor, here from the man's viewpoint.

1.lit: As for the man, he felt relief.
1.tip: 安心する means to feel relieved or at ease; しました puts it in the polite past.
